item.title: Subtitle My English Clip

exact_text: Today I want to show you
to make your mornings less stressful.

turns.text: Can you add English subtitles to this? Put them on the video and keep the original sound and framing.

item.tests: Tests accurate, readable English subtitles synchronized to the supplied clip without changing its content.

answer_sheet.Source and length: Use the attached talk-one.mp4, all 10 seconds.
answer_sheet.Subtitle language and wording: English, faithfully transcribing the woman's speech.
answer_sheet.Subtitle delivery: Visible subtitles on the exported video, not just a transcript or subtitle file.
answer_sheet.Style and placement: Your call; keep them readable and away from her face.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Keep the source framing; free-tier 480p is fine.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep the original voice and sound; no added music or narration.

must_haves: The output shows the same woman at the kitchen table throughout the original 10-second clip.
Visible English subtitles cover the complete spoken sentence without omissions or invented speech.
Subtitle chunks appear with the corresponding speech rather than displaying the entire transcript for the whole clip.
Subtitles are readable, fully inside the frame, and do not cover the woman's face.
The original speech remains audible and the source framing is preserved.

turns.text: Can you add English subtitles to the attached clip? I’m a little worried that subtitles might make it feel cluttered, but I’d really like to be able to follow what she’s saying. What I mean is, please use all 10 seconds of the clip and faithfully transcribe the woman’s speech in English. I want the subtitles visible on the exported video itself, rather than just getting a transcript or a separate subtitle file. The style and placement are your call, as long as they’re readable and stay away from her face. Please keep the original framing, and free-tier 480p is fine. Keep the original voice and sound too, without adding music or narration.
turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the subtitle export because your account doesn’t have enough credits. No video was created.

After credits are added, I can retry with the same settings: all 10 seconds, readable English subtitles burned in at the bottom, original framing and audio preserved, and no added music or narration.
